title: About Me
text:
Ultimately, my goal is to contribute to the conservation of wildlife and their habitats while also spreading awareness of animal welfare and conservation issues with the public. In recent years, that has meant volunteering weekly, taking on relevant internships, and learning as much as, so I can cultivate adequate knowledge and skills to accomplish. My mid-term goal is to be accepted into a wildlife biology and conservation master’s program and then complete a career transition into the conservation field.



University of New Hampshire: Master’s of Science - Communication Sciences & Disorders, Bachelor’s of Science - Communication Sciences & Disorders
Relevant Coursework:
University of New Hampshire: BIOL 806: Data Analysis with R for the Life Sciences, MEFB Marine Mammal Biology & Conservation, BIOL 755: Biological Oceanography, MEF 501: Introduction to Marine Biology, ZOOL 542: Ornithology.
Keene State College: BIOL 110: Cells & Molecules, BIOL 111: Ecology & Evolution




Clearly Speaking - State and ASHA Certified Speech & Language Pathologist
SEABabel Lab, UNH - Lab volunteer
New Hampshire Turtle Rescue - Wildlife Rehabilitation Technician & Community Volunteer
Seacoast Science Center - Marine Mammal Rescue Intern & Exhibit Hall Volunteer
Zoo New England - Field Work Volunteer
New Hampshire Audubon Society - Project Nighthawk Volunteer
Kitty Rescue & Adoption - Community Volunteer
Thanks for checking out my web site!
